subject: Throughput assurance: tokens/sec, p99 latency targets, and commit sizing for Dedicated pools
messages:
From: Claire Turner <claire@edgeware.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgeware.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees — initial questions

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Edgeware is nearing a vendor selection for inference hosting and the procurement team asked me to get concrete throughput & latency guarantees for the Dedicated offering so we can bake them into the SOW. A few specific asks:

- We must have a documented tokens/sec and requests/sec guarantee for our reserved GPU pool (for steady-state load). Please include p95/p99 latency targets and the exact measurement methodology you expect to use.
- How do you size the GPU pool vs committed vCPU/GPU units? We need an example: if we commit X GPUs, what aggregate tokens/sec can we expect for typical LLMs (65B / 13B-class) and at what concurrency levels?
- What are acceptance criteria for on-boarding (test windows, sample payloads), and how are SLA credits calculated if you miss targets?

Procurement also asked about the trade-off between committed capacity (discounts) and the tightness of the SLA — e.g. higher commit -> stronger guaranteed throughput. Can you send a short proposal + measurement plan we can include in our SOW?

Regards,
Claire
Director, Platform Engineering
Edgeware AI

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Turner <claire@edgeware.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees — initial questions

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the clear list. I put together a concise proposal and a measurement plan attached (dedicated-throughput-methodology-v1.pdf) and a pricing sketch (commit-pricing-sheet.xlsx). High level summary below so procurement can get a quick read:

Proposal highlights
- SLO slate: tokens/sec (aggregate per-pool), requests/sec (RPS), and latency SLOs. For <256 token responses we offer p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms at steady-state under the guaranteed throughput.
- Example sizing: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (our mid-tier Dedicated slab) -> baseline measured aggregate throughput 95k–130k tokens/sec for 13B-like models (variable by context length); with mixed short+long workloads we target a conservative guarantee of 75k tokens/sec to account for KV-cache hit variability.
- Per-tenant guarantee: we partition the pool logically; for the commit size Edgeware requested (dedicated pool equivalent to 1/4 slab in our model) we would guarantee 18k tokens/sec and up to 350 requests/sec for median 32-token responses.
- Measurement methodology: three-stage acceptance (dry run, synthetic replay, production shadowing) with a 72-hour acceptance window. Latency measured end-to-end from Edgeware’s egress point to model response, p95/p99 computed on end-to-end latencies after KV-cache warmup.
- Credits: SLA credits based on % of SLA shortfall over monthly windows (sliding 90-day lookback for systemic issues). We propose a credit banding: 0–5% shortfall: 5% monthly credit; 5–15%: 15% credit; >15%: 30% credit or the right to terminate the contract with 30 days notice.

Pricing/commits (sketch)
- 12-month commit: 28% off list for the pool, 6-month: 18% off. We are open to further discounting tied to larger commits or longer terms.

Next steps
1) Internal sizing review (Ben/Laura) — confirm the 18k tokens/sec per-tenant guarantee for the commit Edgeware specified.
2) If confirmed, I’ll send a redlined SLA paragraph for the SOW and a draft acceptance-test plan for procurement.

Thanks — attaching the files.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Edgeware sizing + discount ask

Looping in Rishi for infra validation and Laura for commercial. Quick notes from my side after skimming Nikhil's draft:

- The 18k tokens/sec per-tenant guarantee seems conservative for 1/4 slab but acceptable as a guaranteed floor. We should show a measured 95th percentile baseline so procurement sees headroom — e.g., measured peak 25k tokens/sec per tenant on our benchmark (32-token responses, KV cache warm).
- Measurement: add explicit guidance for model variants and sequence-length profiles. We should define two workload classes for acceptance: "short" (<=64 tokens, 70% of requests) and "mixed" (10% long tail >512 tokens). The acceptance testing should require a representative sample of each class.
- Pricing pushback: procurement will likely ask for 35% off for a 12-month commit plus marketplace credits. Recommend we offer 30% max if they accept a 14-day escalation SLA response target and include a 3-month ramp credit if they exceed a 5% usage burst above commit in months 1–3. That lets us preserve margin while giving their team comfort.

Action: Rishi — can you confirm the measurement harness and whether the 72-hour window + warmup is sufficient operationally?

Ben
Head of Sales Operations
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jan 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Edgeware sizing + discount ask

Ben / team — quick infra confirmation:

- Measurement harness: we will run a three-step validation as Nikhil suggested. Details:
  1) Dry-run (sanity): smoke tests to validate model variant compatibility and baseline throughput at low concurrency. (~4 hours)
  2) Synthetic replay: replay a captured sample of Edgeware traffic at scaled rates (both token- and request-centric tests) to measure tokens/sec and RPS. Include KV-cache warmup phase of 30 minutes, then a 10-hour measurement window for steady-state metrics.
  3) Production shadowing: route a subset (5–10%) of live traffic for 72 hours to validate real-world performance and capture p95/p99.

- Latency measurement: define end-to-end latency from Edgeware client egress to Redwood response arrival. For internal calculation we also record server-side model latency and queueing times but SLOs will be on end-to-end numbers.

- Acceptance thresholds: recommend we publish both conservative guaranteed numbers (what we commit in the SOW) and operational targets (what we expect). This avoids overpromising while giving procurement a clear expectation.

- Credits/thresholds: operationally we can automate credit calculations monthly using our telemetry; the thresholds Nikhil proposed are implementable.

I'll drop a short operations appendix to the PDF to make the measurement steps explicit.

-Rishi
Director, Inference Reliability
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Turner <claire@edgeware.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, procurement@edgeware.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Throughput assurance proposal + acceptance plan (Edgeware AI)

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the questions and for patience while we validated the details with engineering and sales ops. Attached is a final, short proposal and the acceptance/measurement plan (dedicated-throughput-methodology-v1.pdf) for inclusion in the SOW. Key points for procurement:

- Guaranteed numbers (what we will put in SOW):
  • Pool-level aggregate tokens/sec guarantee: 75,000 tokens/sec for the 4-GPU slab baseline (this is pool-wide, not per-tenant).
  • Per-tenant guaranteed throughput for the commit Edgeware discussed (quarter-slab logical partition): 18,000 tokens/sec and up to 350 requests/sec for median 32-token responses.
  • Latency SLOs (end-to-end): p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms for responses <= 256 tokens under guaranteed throughput.

- Measurement & acceptance summary:
  1) Dry run (sanity) — internal kickoff, validate model variants (2–4 hours).
  2) Synthetic replay — 30-minute KV warmup then 10-hour steady-state measurement window; synthetic profile will include short (<=64 tokens, ~70%), medium (65–256 tokens, ~25%), and long (>256, ~5%) distributions.
  3) Production shadowing — 72-hour shadow at 5–10% traffic to validate end-to-end metrics.
  4) Final acceptance: if measured p99/p95 and tokens/sec meet guarantees for the steady-state window, pool is declared accepted. If shortfalls occur, we follow the credit banding and remediation plan in the PDF.

- Commercial trade-offs: we can offer a 12-month commit at 28% off list. If Edgeware wants 35% we can approach that only with a 24-month commit or by moving the pool to a shared-dedicated model (higher isolation but different pricing). As Ben noted, we can offer up to 30% for 12 months if Edgeware accepts a 14-day escalation SLA and the 3-month usage ramp credit clause.

Please review and share any edits you want in the SOW paragraph — happy to jump on a call tomorrow to finalize.

Best,
Nikhil
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
